ov: Tailed amphibians with slender, lizard-like bodies and moist skin, which keeps them near water or damp places. They are best known for regrowing lost limbs and other body parts.

why.dg: Some species’ skin contains the powerful poison tetrodotoxin, advertised by bright warning colours.
why.ac: Most salamanders' eyes are adapted mainly for seeing at night.

rg: Mostly the Northern Hemisphere, richest in eastern North America; some in Central and South America.
fx: Salamanders never have more than four toes on their front feet.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact (some have no lungs) is confirmed: lungless salamanders breathe through their skin and mouth.
